overview.text: Anthropic is a San Francisco-based AI company organized as a public benefit corporation, founded in January 2021 by a group of former OpenAI researchers including siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei. It builds the Claude family of models and describes itself as an AI safety and research company that treats safety as a systematic engineering discipline rather than an afterthought.

citations.quote: an AI safety and research company

what_theyve_done.text: Anthropic was founded in January 2021 by seven former OpenAI employees after disagreements over the direction of AI development there.

citations.quote: founded in January 2021 by seven former employees of OpenAI

what_theyve_done.text: It shipped its first public Claude model in March 2023 and has iterated through the Claude 2, 3, 3.5 and 4 generations since, each adding longer context, tool use and stronger coding performance.

citations.quote: In May 2025, Anthropic released Claude 4 Opus and Sonnet

what_theyve_done.text: In June 2026 it released Claude Sonnet 5, its most agentic mid-tier model yet, alongside Claude Fable 5 and the restricted Claude Mythos 5 as its current top-tier flagship pair, with Fable 5 becoming generally available on June 9, 2026 with a 1-million-token context window on by default.

citations.quote: a 1M token context window by default
built to be the most agentic Sonnet model yet

what_theyve_done.text: On June 12, 2026 the US government applied export controls to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, and Anthropic disabled both models for all customers to comply. Fable 5 returned for everyone on July 1 with a new safety classifier, but Mythos 5 was restored only for a set of US organizations under Anthropic's Glasswing program.

citations.quote: On Friday, June 12, the US government applied export controls to our newest models

what_theyve_done.text: On July 24, 2026 it added Claude Opus 5 to the lineup, priced and positioned between Fable 5 and Sonnet 5. Anthropic's own docs describe it as built for complex agentic coding and enterprise work, at roughly half Fable 5's per-token price for capability the company says comes close to it.

citations.quote: For complex agentic coding and enterprise work

strengths.text: Anthropic trains its models under a published Constitutional AI methodology, aligning them to an explicit written set of principles rather than relying solely on human feedback.

citations.quote: to adhere to a set of principles called a constitution

strengths.text: Its Sonnet 5 release is built around agentic workflows -- planning, autonomous tool use across browsers and terminals, and long-running coding sessions -- rather than one-shot chat.

citations.quote: It can make plans, use tools like browsers and terminals

current_focus.text: Anthropic's current lineup spans four models: Claude Fable 5 at the top tier (its Mythos 5 sibling remains restricted to a set of US organizations following a June 2026 export-control action), Claude Opus 5 next, and Claude Sonnet 5 as the cheaper mid-tier option. Anthropic's own pricing table lists Opus 5 at $5/$25 per million input/output tokens, between Fable 5's $10/$50 and Sonnet 5's $3/$15, and the company's own developer guidance still points users who need maximum capability at Fable 5. Opus 4.8, the prior Opus-branded flagship, has moved to a "Legacy models" table in Anthropic's own docs.

citations.quote: its performance is close to that of Opus 4.8
